open_questions: Who played on which Motown record: Motown credited no musicians until 1971. The credits here are Wikipedia's; Brian Holland (1982) put Benny Benjamin on most of the Supremes' and Four Tops' records and was unsure of Baby Love. Allan Slutsky's Standing in the Shadows of Motown (1989) was not read.
Wikipedia's Allen article also lists Signed, Sealed, Delivered I'm Yours and Marvin Gaye's I Heard It Through the Grapevine, which other sources give to Uriel Jones; not scored here.

His shuffles, which Holland and Uriel Jones single out: How Sweet It Is's only human tab is James Taylor's version, The Way You Do the Things You Do's only tab is machine-made. Transcribe them from the records.
Baby Love's only tab is played in, not gridded; its bars here are read to the beat.
Reach Out I'll Be There's galloping intro: the tab puts it on his snare; Paul Riser overdubbed a pattern with timpani mallets on a tambourine head, which may be it.
Where his nickname came from, and where he was born: not found in the sources read.

identity.name: Richard 'Pistol' Allen

evidence.note: Of cancer, aged 69, four months before Standing in the Shadows of Motown was released.

identity.summary: The Funk Brothers' drummer on most of Holland-Dozier-Holland's Motown hits of the 1960s: Heat Wave, Where Did Our Love Go, Baby Love, Reach Out I'll Be There. A jazz drummer by taste (Max Roach, Buddy Rich), told by Benny Benjamin to hold down simple beats, he was Motown's shuffle man ('the best at the shuffles', Brian Holland) and played light, steady time: the hat open on every beat, the snare or a cross-stick on every beat for a dance record, a short pickup into the phrase. He appeared in Standing in the Shadows of Motown and died in 2002, before it opened.

traditions.impact: Max Roach and Buddy Rich among his influences; Benjamin told him to leave the jazz drumming at home on Motown dates.

formative_events.event: Joins the Funk Brothers at Hitsville after Benjamin ("Pistol came in after Benny": Brian Holland).
Heat Wave, Martha and the Vandellas: Holland-Dozier-Holland's first big hit, and his shuffle.
Where Did Our Love Go and Baby Love, the Supremes' first two number ones.
Plays and speaks in Standing in the Shadows of Motown; dies in June, before its release.

eras.label: Holland-Dozier-Holland's records
eras.context: Hitsville U.S.A., Detroit: the Funk Brothers with James Jamerson, cutting Holland-Dozier-Holland's singles for Martha and the Vandellas, the Supremes and the Four Tops, Benjamin and Uriel Jones sharing the dates.
defining_traits: the hat open on every beat
the snare or a cross-stick on every beat
a short pickup on the snare

evidence.note: Not measured: the records were beat-tracked for tempo only.

swing.notes: Straight eighths on three of the four records scored; Baby Love's eighths swing (the record's hats near a triplet). Holland calls him the shuffle man.

dynamics.balance: A light backbeat or a cross-stick under the singers, the tambourine and the foot stomps on the beat beside him.

feel_profile.interaction: Under Holland-Dozier-Holland's arrangements with Jamerson's bass, beside a tambourine, hand claps or foot stomps on the beat.

hand_techniques.name: The hat open on every beat
hand_techniques.description: Heat Wave's verses: an open hat on each beat over a light backbeat.

hand_techniques.name: The snare on every beat
hand_techniques.description: Reach Out I'll Be There's verses and choruses; Baby Love's cross-stick on every beat.

hand_techniques.name: The pickup
hand_techniques.description: Three or four notes on the snare from the "and" or the "a" of 3 into the next phrase (Heat Wave, Where Did Our Love Go, Baby Love).

foot_techniques.name: The kick under the bass
foot_techniques.description: On 1 and 3, or on 1, the "and" of 2, 3 and the "and" of 4 with Jamerson (Where Did Our Love Go).

devices_search.note: None found. Where Did Our Love Go's sextuplet pickups are fills, and Baby Love's swung eighths a feel; no cross-rhythm or metric device in any song or source read.

voice_language.snare: A light backbeat on 2 and 4, or on every beat; a cross-stick on every beat (Baby Love); short pickups.
voice_language.kick: On 1 and 3, or with the bass line's "and"s.
voice_language.toms: Few: the high and floor toms closing Reach Out I'll Be There's chorus fills.
voice_language.hihat: Eighths, or open on every beat (Heat Wave), opened on the "and"s for a lift.
voice_language.cymbals: Hardly a crash: Reach Out I'll Be There's verses and choruses start on one; the ride in quarters for a section of Heat Wave.

aesthetic: a light snare under the tambourine and the stomps

by_era.description: The studio set of Ludwig, Slingerland, Rogers and Gretsch parts; the Where Did Our Love Go tab names a Ludwig Downbeat; a silver sparkle Ludwig in the one photograph.

sample_hints.60s: A 1960s Ludwig, round and warm, close and a little roomy.

signature_traits.label: The shuffle man
signature_traits.description: Brian Holland: 'He was the best at the shuffles'; Uriel Jones: 'noted for the shuffle and the 4/4 beat. He was a genius with it.'

signature_traits.label: The snare on every beat
signature_traits.description: Reach Out I'll Be There's snare and Baby Love's cross-stick on all four beats, for the dance floor.

signature_traits.label: The open hat on the beat
signature_traits.description: Heat Wave's hat open on every beat over a light backbeat.

patterns.name: Heat Wave: the hat open on every beat
patterns.function: The hat open on every beat over the snare on 2 and 4 and the kick on 1 and 3: the verse.

patterns.name: Heat Wave: the pickup
patterns.function: The snare on the "and" of 3, 4 and its "and" into the next phrase, under the open hat.

patterns.name: Where Did Our Love Go: the verse
patterns.function: Eighths on the hat, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1, the "and" of 2, 3 and the "and" of 4, under the foot stomps.

patterns.name: Where Did Our Love Go: the sextuplet pickup
patterns.function: The snare on the "a" of 3, 4, its "e" and its "a": a sextuplet run in the tab, here the nearest sixteenths.

patterns.name: Baby Love: the cross-stick on every beat
patterns.function: Swung eighths on the hat, a cross-stick on every beat, the kick on 1 and 3.

evidence.note: Read to the beat from a tab played in rather than gridded: a reconstruction.

patterns.name: Reach Out I'll Be There: the snare on every beat
patterns.function: The snare on every beat under eighths on the hat, the kick on 1, the "and" of 3 and the "and" of 4.

patterns.name: Reach Out I'll Be There: the gallop
patterns.function: The intro: cross-sticks on 1 and the "e", "and" and "a" of every beat over the kick in eighths (perhaps Paul Riser's overdub of mallets on a tambourine head).

equipment.label: Studio A's kit, 1960s
equipment.layout_notes: A studio set of Ludwig, Slingerland, Rogers and Gretsch parts (Wikipedia); the Where Did Our Love Go tab heads its drum track "Ludwig Downbeat Kit". A silver sparkle Ludwig in the one photograph of him at a kit.

affiliations.name: The Funk Brothers
affiliations.notes: Motown's studio band at Hitsville U.S.A., uncredited on the records until 1971.

evidence.note: Benjamin told him to 'leave the jazz drumming at home, hold down simple beats'.
Jones: 'Pistol was there before I was'; the two shared Motown's dates as Benjamin's health failed.

philosophy.idea: Leave the jazz at home: hold down simple beats (Benjamin's advice to him).

contribution.description: The drum chair on most of Holland-Dozier-Holland's hits, from Heat Wave to Reach Out I'll Be There: the light, steady Motown beat with the snare on every beat, and its shuffles.

innovations: The Supremes' cross-stick on every beat (Baby Love), by the tab

cultural_references.description: Standing in the Shadows of Motown (2002): he plays and speaks in it, and died before it opened.
Michigan Rock and Roll Legends Hall of Fame, 2010, with the Funk Brothers.

common_misconceptions: That Benny Benjamin played every Motown hit: Heat Wave, Where Did Our Love Go and Baby Love are credited to Allen, though Holland (1982) remembered Benjamin on most of the Supremes' records.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A 1960s Ludwig in a small room
generation_rules: A light backbeat, or the snare on every beat for a dance record.
Eighths on the hat, or the hat open on every beat.
A short pickup on the snare into the next phrase; hardly any crashes.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: A jazz drummer by taste after Max Roach and Buddy Rich, simplified on Benny Benjamin's advice into the Motown studio beat, beside Uriel Jones.
